summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-react preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload unrelated to declared purpose
details: The package advertises itself as a Babel React preset (index.js is a 288-byte config), but its package.json preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a shipped `math_init.js` (~727 KB) via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js], { cwd: D })`. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated in the obfuscator.io style (`_0x`-prefixed identifiers, wrapper objects holding all literal strings, a shuffled constant array, and a `WV8StW` string-array rotation routine). Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time to execute a large, obfuscated, cover-story-named blob is unrelated to the declared Babel-preset purpose and matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the fetched Bun binary is used to run attacker-shipped bundled code that Node-oriented scanners in the installer's supply chain are unlikely to trace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
